title: K-injective complexes and K-injective resolutions of sheaves of modules
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site, $\mathcal O$ a sheaf of commutative rings on $\mathcal C$, and $\Mod(\mathcal O)$ the abelian category of sheaves of $\mathcal O$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Two morphisms $f,g:\mathcal K^\bullet\to\mathcal I^\bullet$ of cochain complexes of $\mathcal O$-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules] are *homotopic* if there are morphisms $h^p:\mathcal K^p\to\mathcal I^{p-1}$ of $\mathcal O$-modules with $f^p-g^p=d_{\mathcal I}^{p-1}h^p+h^{p+1}d_{\mathcal K}^p$ for all $p$. A cochain complex $\mathcal I^\bullet$ of $\mathcal O$-modules is *K-injective* if every morphism of complexes $\mathcal K^\bullet\to\mathcal I^\bullet$ from an acyclic complex $\mathcal K^\bullet$ [def-pc-acyclic-complex-modules] is homotopic to zero; equivalently $\operatorname{Hom}_{K(\mathcal O)}(\mathcal K^\bullet,\mathcal I^\bullet)=0$ in the homotopy category for every acyclic $\mathcal K^\bullet$. A *K-injective resolution* of a complex $\mathcal M^\bullet$ is a quasi-isomorphism $\mathcal M^\bullet\to\mathcal I^\bullet$ [def-pc-quasi-iso-modules] with $\mathcal I^\bullet$ K-injective.
